messages:
alice: noticed a throughput drop on the 8xA100 TP+PP staging cluster after yesterday's kernel-selector change. avg seq=512 latency up ~18% and all-reduce time increased.
ben: ugh. any nvprof/nsight captured traces yet? :eyes:
alice: captured a short nvprof run. attaching snippet below from the step where kv-cache merge and linear layer comms overlap badly:
```
GPU activities:
  Allreduce  total_time_ms: 12.3  calls: 64
  GEMM      total_time_ms: 28.1  calls: 64
  MemcpyH2D total_time_ms: 3.2
```
CPU timers (custom):
  kv_merge_ms: 9.8
  prefix_copy_ms: 4.4
  forward_ms: 35.9
```
carol: hm the kernel-selector change forced bf16->fp16 fused kernels on some ranks? that could change compute/comm balance and reduce overlap window.
ben: can you paste the kernel selection log lines? I want to check fallback on smaller seqs.
alice: here are the relevant lines from our selector output:
```
[rank0] sel: attn_kernel=fast_fp16_matmul, type=split_kv, fallback=false
[rank1] sel: attn_kernel=fast_bf16_matmul, type=split_kv, fallback=true
[rank2] sel: attn_kernel=fast_fp16_matmul, type=merge_kv, fallback=false
```
dan: mismatch across ranks is suspicious. if one rank uses bf16 kernels and others fp16, comm payloads/packers may differ and increase allreduce overhead.
carol: also check nvtx ranges — if the memcpy+allreduce NVTX spans are longer on some GPUs that prevents overlap.
ben: suggestion: run a synchronized nsight timeline capture for a single batch with seq=512, batch=2, TP=2, PP=4 and use "nsys profile" with NVTX markers. compare stacks for all ranks.
alice: ran that. timeline shows allreduce starts earlier but stalls at 1.1ms waiting on recv on rank1. timeline link: https://intra.redwood/prof/176982
perf-bot: automated regression detector flagged kernel-selector change as correlated with +15% tail latency on 8x benchmarks.
alice: tried a quick local experiment forcing uniform kernel by env KERNEL_OVERRIDE=fast_fp16_matmul on all ranks -> allreduce time dropped to 9.5ms and overall latency back to baseline.
ben: good repro. two hypotheses:
  - selector produces heterogeneous kernels across partition boundaries
  - pack/unpack or type conversion on rank1 is causing extra memcpy/serialize step
carol: next steps:
  1) add a selector validation unit that ensures chosen kernel family is consistent across TP groups before rolling out.
  2) add a per-rank nvprof micro-benchmark: measure contiguous vs strided pack times for kv cache.
  3) instrument all-reduce wrapper to emit small histogram of wait-before-send and wait-after-send latencies (ms bins)

dan: I can implement (3) quickly — will add two microtimers around the NCCL allreduce call and log per-step metrics to statsd.
ben: for (2) please include a synthetic workload that exercises prefix-copy heavy cases (seq 1024, warm cache) and run 10 iters to average.
alice: I'll run selector-validation on staging and re-run the 8x job after Dan's allreduce timers land. planning to pin selector to fast_fp16_matmul for now to reduce blast radius.
carol: also let's add an alert: if per-step allreduce p50 increases >10% vs baseline for 5 consecutive runs, auto-toggle to safe kernel family.
alice: sounds good. will open a PR with the rollback toggle + selector check and attach the nvprof/nsys artifacts.
ben: thanks Alice, Dan, Carol. small experiment notes: keep nvprof runs short to avoid jitter, prefer nsys timeline for overlap visualization. :thumbsup:
alice: thanks — I'll post the PR and the captured traces to the thread when ready.
